_what: Every tuned number in the pipeline, with what it was fitted on and how many samples. A threshold with no provenance is a guess wearing a lab coat.
_why: 2026-08-08. Two things forced this. (1) engine.py's shot_match_clamp was 'tuned on a NIGHT car edit, one light state end to end' and then silently carried into travel_vlog, which runs golden hour to night by design - it stopped working and nobody changed it. (2) verify 13's duplicate threshold carried its OWN comment saying 'fitted to THREE samples... widen the sample and re-derive before trusting it further' and nobody did, so it passed three duplicates by a hair. His complaint - 'it keeps on happening, especially when i switch frm vlog content to car review' - is partly this: numbers travel between formats when they should not.
_and_this_matters_more: His judgment is the BOOTSTRAP, not the ceiling. The end goal is an agent that scans what is actually winning, measures it, and builds better. When that exists, most of the numbers below get REPLACED by measurements from real winning videos. They are provisional by design. status=provisional means: re-derive me, do not defend me.
_how_to_read: fitted_on = the footage the number came from. samples = how many. status = measured | provisional | guess. pillars = which pillars it is allowed to run on; '*' means genuinely universal and you must justify that.
